card.name: Yemaya dance
card.tagline: Orisha dance honoring Yemaya, goddess of the sea.
card.profile: The Yemaya dance is the Afro-Cuban orisha dance for Yemaya (Yemoja), the Yoruba/Lucumi orisha of the sea and motherhood (syncretized with Our Lady of Regla; color blue), within Santeria/Regla de Ocha ritual and its staged folkloric form. It is performed to bata-drum toques (Yemaya's flowing 6/8) with akpwon/coro call-and-response in Lucumi; the dancer's arms and skirt mimic crashing waves and ocean swells in sweeping, undulating, circular motions, sometimes imitating swimming or diving. Staged by ensembles such as the Conjunto Folklorico Nacional de Cuba (Hakai Magazine; Dancing the Orishas).
card.insight: As scholars note, while Yemaya is honored through dance within Santeria ceremony, Yemaya is not a dance in itself - it is an orisha, and the dance is one component of orisha worship and possession ritual (Hakai Magazine).
card.image_significance: Orisha dance of the sea-mother. A representative image shows ceremonial regalia in a ritual context — imagery should be handled respectfully, not as spectacle — Santeria, Cuba.
